{ "markdown": "# Development Requirements Documentn n---n n## **Background**n nQuantifying the guanine-plus-cytosine (G+C) content of nucleotide sequences is a fundamental operation in molecular biology and genomics workflows. Real-world sequence data may be DNA or RNA, may mix upper and lower case letters, and may include IUPAC ambiguity codes that represent uncertain bases. Because ambiguous symbols can be interpreted in several ways — excluded from the calculation, counted only in the denominator, or statistically weighted — a GC-content utility must offer explicit, deterministic strategies for handling them, and must reject unsupported strategies rather than silently producing misleading values.
